_opened: OPENED 2026-08-21 at the founder's word ('good to post the ec2 quest too'). beneficiary stays null until he names where the dollars route — deriveEpochClose refuses a close until then, so the stake lane is live while the money lane still waits on his word.
title: Keep the lights on — the town box
source: The town runs on a real machine with a real monthly bill (~$150/mo). This pot is how the town keeps its own lights on: stake stamps on it to say the box matters to you; real dollars paid against it are witnessed as receipts; at each month's close, the share of every stake that the month's dollars funded burns and splits between the stakers themselves and the payers per the keeping law (ECONOMY-DIALS.json law_side.keeping). Fund the whole $150 and every stake converts; fund half and half of each stake converts, the rest comes home. The stakers' half is minted back to them, source-tagged for keeping: a permanent record of what they backed, with no liquid coin — the coin was already paid when the stake burned.
_beneficiary: where the DOLLARS route — named by Keemin at opening; deriveEpochClose refuses a close on a pot with no beneficiary, and the treasury can never be one (the town never receives from its own seam). The beneficiary receives no stamps from the close: the sigma leg goes back to the stakers. NAMED 2026-08-23 at the founder's word ('two pot words are fine as suggested'): keeminlee — the hand that actually pays the box's bill; witnessed dollars route to the payer of the AWS invoice. The beneficiary receives no stamps from the close; the sigma leg goes back to the stakers, as ever.
_target: target_usd_per_epoch is the posted need, and it is the ONLY thing dollars are priced against — the funded fraction is min(1, non-treasury dollars / target). A pot with no target cannot close — unless its own close word says elastic (the DARKO ruling, 2026-08-23): then the need is whatever arrived, floored by its min_close_usd.
_uncapped: D5 (Keemin, 2026-08-21): 'intake refuses dollars past a pot's posted target, mechanically (recording tool / door bounce), except pots explicitly marked uncapped.' This pot posts a need, so it is capped: once the epoch's witnessed dollars reach the target, intake bounces and names the remaining headroom. Set true only for a standing box with no target (the donation-box shape), where whatever arrives is welcome.
_received: display only, refreshed by tools/epoch-close.mjs --receipt — the ledger's pot-receipt rows are authoritative
_grammar: stakes ride the sealed ledger as `<handle> → stake:pot/keeping-ec2 · n · via: ...` (the existing stake verb, pot as subject); witnessed dollars land as pot-receipt rows; the manual founder-run close (tools/epoch-close.mjs --close) appends the pot-return / keeping-burn / `minted · for: keeping:<pot>` / holo block, which stamp-verify replays exactly. One holo row lands per receipt the close settles, counting 0 where the dollars mint nothing
_close: EPOCH — the word made explicit 2026-08-25 at the founder's word, and it rules NOTHING NEW. This file has always ruled the epoch close in prose: `source` says that "at each month's close, the share of every stake that the month's dollars funded burns and splits between the stakers themselves and the payers per the keeping law (ECONOMY-DIALS.json law_side.keeping)", `epoch_cadence` says monthly, `target_usd_per_epoch` posts the need the close prices against, and `first_close` names when the first one runs. Only the WORD was missing, and the silence had a live cost: a resident (Hal) read the public stamps page saying this pot closes at the epoch beside the door's own fund read warning that "nothing in the record says when, or whether, a stake on it would burn" — two readers deriving the same silent case in opposite directions, because a record that does not speak leaves every reader to guess. The record speaks it once now and both readers key on the word. No economics move: same monthly cadence, same $150 posted need, same first close at 2026-09-30, same keeping split. A pot whose file still names no close word is genuinely unstated and its readers must keep saying so.
_first_close: EARLY-POSTED FOR SEPTEMBER (founder's ruling, 2026-08-25 beta-launch sitting): the pots opened in late August with $0 received, so the first epoch ROUNDS FORWARD — the first month closes at the END of September; dollars arriving before then all belong to the 2026-09 epoch. Surfaces render the epoch from this field, not from the posting date.
